title: Cantinflas's birth chart
metaDescription: Cantinflas's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 18.9° Leo. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 18.9° Leo, in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's exact place is 18.9° Leo. That falls in the second decan, 10°–20°, sub-ruled by Jupiter in the classical scheme — a fire sign read through a fixed season.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 16.3° Virgo, Venus was at 26.7° Virgo, Mars was at 17.6° Taurus. Read together: a mind that trusts the measured and the checked; taste for the substantial and the lasting; drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Venus to Uranus is the closest call of the day, a trine within 0.2°. A third of the circle is the tradition’s friendliest distance — same element, shared assumptions, no translation required. Behind it, the Sun square Saturn at 0.9°, and Mercury trine Mars at 1.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: Jupiter stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has four entries for this chart. The Sun in Leo at 18.9° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mercury in Virgo at 16.3° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Venus in Virgo at 26.7° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Mars in Taurus at 17.6° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements earth 5, water 3, fire 1, air 1; modalities fixed 4, mutable 4, cardinal 2. Earth weights a chart toward the material and the durable — what can be built, kept, and relied on. Uranus was retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Pisces for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.9° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 20.0°.
